text: Nobody tells you why I R E D A fell fifty seven percent, while its new loans jumped thirty one percent. Multibagger, or trap?
I R E D A listed in November 2023, at an issue price of thirty two rupees. By July 2024, it hit three hundred ten. Almost ten times, in eight months.
Today it's near one hundred thirty two. Fifty seven percent below the top. So what does it actually do?
It's the government's green energy lender. It borrows, and lends to solar, wind and clean power projects. And here's the twist. The business kept growing.
Latest quarter. Income up fourteen percent. New loans up thirty one percent. Net bad loans down from two percent, to one point one.
But profit grew just one percent. Interest costs rose thirteen percent, and bad loan provisions almost tripled.

And there's more. Six hundred seventy three crore of loans are tagged as fraud, linked to Gensol. A 2025 Q I P cut the government's stake below seventy two percent. And the stock trades at two and a half times book value.
So, multibagger or trap? Neither, for now. At three hundred ten, the price ran far ahead of the business. Now lending grows fast, but profit doesn't. Watch bad loans and borrowing costs.
Save this, and send it to your friend who bought I R E D A near the top. Education only, not investment advice. Follow money in cloud.
